comments.note: orchestrator-manager.ts re-exports formatProgressEntry via 'export { formatProgressEntry } from ...' — this is clean but means callers that import it from orchestrator-manager.ts will now pick up the new module path transitively. No issue for current callers; worth documenting if orchestrator-manager.ts is ever split further.

The EMPTY_RESOLUTION sentinel in resolve-progress.ts is a frozen object literal — it's safe because spread ({ ...EMPTY_RESOLUTION, logFilename }) is used everywhere instead of mutating it, so there's no aliasing risk. Adding Object.freeze() would make this intent explicit but is optional at build-time.

comments.note: Theoretical slug-suffix collision: resolveProgress() matches log files by name.endsWith('-{slug}.jsonl'). If slug 'B' is a string suffix of another slug 'A' (e.g. 'feat' vs 'my-feat'), files for 'A' would also match a query for 'feat'. In practice, slugs are full ISO-date-prefixed strings (e.g. '2026-05-06-feature-name') making accidental suffix overlap extremely unlikely. No action required, but worth documenting in resolve-progress.ts if slug format ever becomes less structured.

No test for a 0-byte (empty) log file. The implementation handles it correctly (empty string → split produces no non-empty lines → falls through to EMPTY_RESOLUTION with logFilename populated), but this path is not exercised by the test suite.
